messages:
jess: Hey team — customer hit a hard parse failure when using structured output (they're in "json-mode" streaming). Appended the minimal repro and error. Started after a small client change that interleaves temp ids into item objects. Error from our API: `parse_error: invalid JSON at byte 387 (unexpected token)`

jess: Repro steps: 1) POST to /v1/generate with header `X-Redwood-Mode: structured_json` and `stream: true`. 2) payload has top-level array `items` where some elements are partial objects (missing required `id`), others include `temp_id` extras. 3) client retries on socket timeout which sometimes concatenates frames.

jess: Example (redacted):
```
{
  "items": [
    {"id": "item-1", "price": 100},
    {"temp_id": "t-42", "price": 50},
    {"id": "item-3", "price": 0}  
  ]
}
```

jess: Response body we returned (truncated):
```
...
{"items":[{"id":"item-1","status":"ok"},{"id":"item-3","status":"ok"}

parse_error: unexpected end of input
```

amanda-support: Thanks — sorry for the hit. Can you paste the request_id/req_id and a full raw capture of the streaming frames? Also need customer org id to check billing spike. I'll triage. :handshake:

jess: req_id=req_7f9a. Raw capture attached (pasted below) — you'll see frames arriving like: `...]}
{"items":[{"temp_id":"t-42","price":50},` (i.e., an object starting in the middle of array). Customer org: acme-ops-77. Latency note: they saw a lot of retries, billing jump ~3x over baseline.

ryan-eng: Looking. Initial thought: the combination of streaming + client-side partial objects (temp_id) + retries concatenating frames can produce invalid stream boundaries for our JSON-mode parser. If we treat top-level array as chunk-delimited, a trailing partial object can cause an unexpected token when the following frame begins with `{` without a separating comma.

ryan-eng: Can you include the exact Content-Length and any intermediate chunk separators from the raw TCP capture? Also, do you have the model response mode set to `json_array` vs `json_stream`? That changes how we expect separators.

jess: Content-Lengths from capture: frames were ~512b and ~189b. Example raw sequence (newlines kept):
```
...},{"id":"item-1","status":"ok"}
[{"temp_id":"t-42","price":50},
{"id":"item-3","status":"ok"}]
```

jess: Note the client mistakenly sent an opening `[` in the middle of stream on retry. Customer code re-opens array instead of continuing with comma.

mila-billing: Noted org acme-ops-77. I'll flag billing: spike starts 2025-10-28T14:02Z to 14:20Z. Need timeline + peak usage for charge dispute. Please DM me the full request IDs.

sam-sre: Adding incident tag. I'll open INC-2025-342 and link this thread. If this is a common client bug we should add defensive parsing or clearer SDK guidance.

ryan-eng: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) in the short term, fallback to tolerant parsing for streaming inputs from this org (try to auto-repair when we detect an extra `[` or missing comma at frame boundary) — feasible but risky. 2) better: push SDK patch and docs to ensure clients don't re-open arrays on retry. 3) server-side: validate chunk framing and reject early with a clear error (so client can fix instead of retrying blindly).

amanda-support: For the customer, ask them to: a) stop automatic retry for streaming requests, b) update client to use buffered single-request mode for now, or c) update to the patched SDK we'll produce. I'll send recommended language.

jess: Customer confirmed they can toggle retries off for streaming. They're okay to apply workaround for now but want a permanent fix — especially since they hit billing surge.

ryan-eng: I'll reproduce locally. Can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces the broken interleaving? If not, I'll synthesize with two writes to a single socket to emulate the retry behavior.

jess: Minimal repro (synthesized):
```bash
# open a raw connection and write two successive frames to simulate retry concat
printf '{"items":[{"id":"item-1","price":100}]' | nc host 443
# then immediately write a second payload without the leading comma
printf '[{"temp_id":"t-42","price":50},{"id":"item-3","price":0}]' | nc host 443
```

ryan-eng: Perfect — reproduces here. Parser throws at merged boundary. I'll propose a small parser change to treat an unexpected `[` after `]` or `}` as a recoverable comma insertion if it occurs exactly at a frame boundary, gated by org id allowlist. Will write a PR and request opt-in for acme-ops-77 while we test.

mila-billing: Once we have opt-in, we can credit the spike window for acme-ops-77 pending root cause. Keep me posted.

amanda-support: I'll notify the customer about the opt-in plan and the temporary mitigation steps. Thanks everyone — tagging @ryan-eng for the PR and @sam-sre to monitor deployment. :white_check_mark:
